method: PRODUCED - CONSUMED symbol parity (rg across src/, bin/, interfaces/, shared/), read-before-write triage

findings.produced: pub struct EventBus (empty marker) + pub fn EventBus::new(), re-exported as pub use bus::EventBus
findings.rationale: rg -n 'event::EventBus\b|event::\{[^}]*EventBus\b' over src/, bin/, interfaces/, shared/ returns no production caller. rg -n 'EventBus::new()' shows every other match is GatewayEventBus::new() or TopologyEventBus::new(), not the bare event::EventBus. The doc-comment claim that commands/start/mod.rs constructs EventBus::new() is false — verified via rg -n 'event::' src/bin/aleph-server/commands/start/mod.rs which shows only EventContext, EventFilter, EventHandler, EventType, GlobalBus imports.
findings.proposed_change: Delete src/event/bus.rs; remove 'mod bus;' and 'pub use bus::EventBus;' from src/event/mod.rs; update module-level doc to drop the EventBus bullet.
findings.risk: low. No external consumer exists (rg proves this). Worst case is an interface we missed; the broad rg rules that out.
findings.verification: After cut, rg -n 'EventBus' src/ bin/ interfaces/ shared/ should not reference the bare event::EventBus type. cargo check -p alephcore (out of scope per task) should succeed.

findings.produced: pub fn GlobalBus::subscribe (sync, blocking) — distinct from subscribe_async
findings.rationale: rg -n '\.subscribe\(filter|GlobalBus::global\(\)\.subscribe\(' src/ bin/ interfaces/ shared/ shows every .subscribe() call is on GatewayEventBus or TopologyEventBus, never on GlobalBus. The only mention of GlobalBus::subscribe is the doc-comment at global_bus.rs:23. Every live producer-side subscriber uses subscribe_async (e.g. teams/dispatcher/mod.rs:236, gateway/announce_delivery.rs:94, teams/notifier.rs boot path).
findings.proposed_change: Delete src/event/global_bus.rs:283-306 and the doc-comment block at global_bus.rs:23-28.
findings.risk: low. Removing it also closes a latent footgun: the implementation calls tokio::task::block_in_place which would panic if invoked outside a runtime with block_in_place support.
findings.verification: rg -n 'GlobalBus::global\(\)\.subscribe\b|bus\.subscribe\(filter' src/ bin/ interfaces/ shared/ returns zero hits after the cut.

findings.produced: pub struct Subscription { pub id: SubscriptionId, pub filter: EventFilter, pub callback: Arc<dyn Fn(GlobalEvent) + Send + Sync> }
findings.consumer_location: src/event/global_bus.rs:259-264 (internal: sub.filter.matches, Arc::clone(&sub.callback) inside broadcast); no external code reads these fields
findings.rationale: rg -n 'Subscription\s*\{' over src/, bin/, interfaces/, shared/ shows that event::Subscription is constructed only inside subscribe/subscribe_async (global_bus.rs:289, 314); fields are read only by broadcast (global_bus.rs:259-264). No external code constructs or inspects event::Subscription. The fields could be private without breaking any caller.
findings.proposed_change: Change pub id, pub filter, pub callback to private in src/event/global_bus.rs:164-168. Keep the type pub for the Debug impl. Optionally remove Subscription from the pub use in src/event/mod.rs:29 if no external code references it.
findings.risk: low. External consumers cannot be relying on these fields (rg confirms zero reads).
findings.verification: rg -n 'Subscription\b' src/ bin/ interfaces/ shared/ after the change shows event::Subscription only inside src/event/global_bus.rs.

findings.rationale: Zero external callers for either method. The internal HashMap uses SubscriptionId's Hash/Eq; external code that needs to format/inspect the id uses Display or Deref<Target=str>.
